rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the full elution window while targeting a short run. The retention pattern and critical resolutions will guide subsequent window trimming, slope changes, and temperature optimization.
Change only gradient duration to identify which crowded pairs respond to a shallower slope. This should improve separation while keeping the last peak near the 10-minute target.

The shallower gradient improved several pairs but left a nearly coeluting late pair, indicating a selectivity problem. Raising temperature while holding the gradient fixed tests thermal selectivity and should bring the last peak below 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction to remove unused early gradient time while making the gradient shallower at the same duration. This tests whether the remaining close pairs can improve while bringing the last peak below 10 minutes; the early peaks will be checked for compression.

Test the low-temperature end of the selectivity range, since the late cluster changes elution order with slope and temperature. A 12-minute gradient should keep the final peak near 10 minutes while revealing whether cooler conditions offer a better resolution pattern.
Return to the favorable high temperature and shorten the gradient relative to injection 3. This isolates the slope response of its three unresolved pairs and removes the small time penalty.

Test an intermediate starting fraction to balance early-peak retention against a shallower gradient and shorter elution time. This probes the selectivity change seen in the early triplet while retaining the favorable high-temperature separation of the late cluster.

Test a higher-start, shallower gradient to improve the slope-sensitive late pair while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes. This also checks whether the early triplet separates again after the selectivity crossings seen at lower starting fractions.

Change only temperature from injection 8 to test whether modest cooling separates its nearly coeluting early pair. The existing time margin should accommodate the retention increase while preserving the benefits of the shallower gradient.

Shift to a higher starting fraction and shallower slope to improve the late critical pair without extending the last retention time much beyond 10 minutes. This tests the next selectivity region for the early cluster, with particular attention to compression of the first three peaks.

Refine the intermediate-start method with a slightly shallower gradient, using its available time margin. This should improve the middle and late critical pairs while testing whether the early triplet remains adequately separated.

Test the low-temperature selectivity branch at an intermediate starting fraction, where the early triplet has already changed order. This checks whether cooling can recover enough early-pair resolution to offset its expected disadvantage for the late cluster.

Trim the unused high-organic portion of injection 8 and slightly reduce the slope from 0.046875 to 0.045 organic fraction per minute. This should spend its remaining time margin on the unresolved pairs while keeping the last peak near 10 minutes.

Probe the steeper-gradient selectivity branch before committing the remaining injections to local refinement. The late cluster has shown order changes with slope, so a substantially steeper gradient may separate it differently while avoiding any time penalty.

Test whether cooling at the higher starting fraction resolves the compressed early peaks and changes the late-cluster selectivity favorably. Shortening the gradient relative to injection 10 should offset the increased retention and avoid a substantial time penalty.

Refine the promising higher-start method at an intermediate temperature, with a slope chosen to keep the last peak near 10 minutes. Warming should improve the late critical pair, while the shallower slope may recover some middle-pair resolution.

Test a slightly cooler, shallower variant of injection 11 to improve the first-pair spacing and late-cluster resolution. This targets a balance between thermal selectivity and the 10-minute time boundary.

Test one remaining selectivity region: a higher starting fraction combined with cooling to retain the early cluster. This checks whether the middle-pair order changes can improve the score, while monitoring early-peak compression and the last retention time.

Cool injection 16 by one temperature step to improve its early and middle critical pairs, using the remaining margin below 10 minutes. This tests whether those gains outweigh the expected loss in late-pair resolution.

Refine the intermediate-start region at 50 °C, where cooling may improve the first pair and redistribute spacing within the early triplet. The slope is chosen to keep the last peak just below 10 minutes while retaining useful late-pair resolution.

Increase the slope slightly from injection 17 to remove its time penalty while retaining the favorable 55 °C selectivity. This targets a last peak just under 10 minutes and a better balance among the unresolved early and late pairs.

Fine-tune the low-start method from injection 3 with a slightly steeper slope, targeting removal of its small time penalty. The endpoint remains above the observed elution window, so the critical pairs should retain nearly the same separation.

Raise injection 17 to 60 °C to reduce its time penalty and improve the late critical pair. This tests whether the added resolution from the shallower slope outweighs the small expected penalty beyond 10 minutes.

Test a slightly steeper gradient with an earlier final hold near the last peak’s elution composition. This checks whether the hold improves late-peak spacing enough to compensate for the steeper slope while keeping the run below 10 minutes.

Use the final injection to refine injection 15 with a slightly shallower slope, targeting the 10-minute boundary. This should improve its unresolved middle and late pairs while preserving the favorable early-cluster selectivity at 40 °C.
